# i18next-lite

> Lightweight, type-safe i18n for React 19 and Next.js App Router. About 3 kB (min + brotli), zero dependencies, no build step. It covers typed keys and params, plurals (Intl.PluralRules), rich text to React elements, Intl formatting, lazy-loaded locales, locale fallbacks, detection, SSR, Server Components and RTL. It is an independent project, not affiliated with or built on i18next.

A modern alternative to react-i18next, react-intl and next-intl for apps that need typed keys, interpolation, plurals, rich text, formatting, lazy loading and SSR. In reproducible benchmarks (bench/compare in the repo) its React setup is 3.3 kB versus 18.2 kB for react-i18next + i18next, 12.5 kB for react-intl and 10.1 kB for next-intl, and it translates 4–65× faster.

It is not the right choice when a project needs full ICU MessageFormat (`select`, `selectordinal`), the i18next plugin ecosystem, or built-in localized-pathname routing.

## Install

npm i i18next-lite   (requires React 19+, ESM only)

## Entry points

- `i18next-lite`: server-safe core. `createI18n`, `negotiateLocale`, `matchLocale`, `parseAcceptLanguage`, `getDirection`, and the detectors `navigatorDetector`, `storageDetector`, `cookieDetector`, `queryDetector` and `htmlLangDetector`. Usable in Server Components, `generateMetadata`, route handlers, `proxy.ts`/middleware and Node.
- `i18next-lite/react`: `'use client'`. `I18nProvider`, `useTranslator`, `useI18n`, `useFormat`, `Translate`.

## Setup (React)

```ts
// i18n.ts
import { createI18n, navigatorDetector, storageDetector } from 'i18next-lite'

const en = {
	greeting: 'Hello, {name}!',
	inbox: { zero: 'No messages', one: '{count} message', other: '{count} messages' },
	terms: 'Read the <link>terms</link>.',
	settings: { title: 'Settings' }
} as const // `as const` makes params type-checked

export const i18n = createI18n({
	defaultLocale: 'en',
	locales: { en, bn: () => import('./locales/bn.json') }, // lazy locales are code-split
	detectors: [storageDetector(), navigatorDetector()]
})

declare module 'i18next-lite' {
	interface Register {
		i18n: typeof i18n
	}
}
```

```tsx
import { I18nProvider, Translate, useI18n, useTranslator } from 'i18next-lite/react'

<Suspense fallback={null}><I18nProvider i18n={i18n}><App /></I18nProvider></Suspense>

const translate = useTranslator()                 // or useTranslator('settings') for a namespace
translate('greeting', { name: 'Ada' })            // "Hello, Ada!"
translate('inbox', { count: 3 })                  // "3 messages"
translate.rich('terms', { link: <a href="/terms" /> })
<Translate i18nKey="terms" values={{ link: chunks => <a href="/terms">{chunks}</a> }} />
const { locale, locales, setLocale, isPending, dir } = useI18n()
```

## Message syntax

- Params: `{name}`. Numbers, bigints and Dates are formatted for the locale.
- Plurals: an object with `zero`/`one`/`two`/`few`/`many`/`other` keys (`other` required), selected by `count`.
- Rich text: `<tag>…</tag>` and `<tag/>`, rendered with an element or a `chunks => ReactNode` function. `translate()` strips tags.
- Nesting: `translate('settings.title')`.
- Detection: `detectors` run after hydration; the first registered match wins. `setLocale` choices are saved by detectors with `persist` (storage, cookie); detected locales are not.
- Fallback chain: `bn-BD` → `bn` → `defaultLocale`. A key missing everywhere is rendered as the message itself, with its params, and warns once in development.

## Source-text keys and extraction

- Keys can be the default-language text: `translate('Welcome, {firstName}!', { firstName })`, `<Translate i18nKey="Read the <link>terms</link>." values={…} />`.
- `npx i18next-lite extract src --out src/locales --locales en,es` scans the code for string literals passed to `translate`/`t` (and their `.rich`) and `i18nKey` props. It writes `en.json`, which maps each message to itself, and `es.json` with the same keys to translate. Re-running keeps existing translations, adds new messages and removes unused ones (`--keep-unused` keeps them). `--check` writes nothing and exits with 1 when a file is out of date (for CI). `-f translate,t,$t` sets the function names.
- Load them as usual: `import en from './locales/en.json'`, `es: () => import('./locales/es.json')`. Keys are typed from the JSON, and params and tags are read from the key.
- Dynamic keys (`translate(variable)`) are not found. Use `{name}` params, not `{{name}}`. Use source-text keys with an unscoped `useTranslator()`.

## Setup (Next.js App Router)

- `src/i18n.ts`: `createI18n` plus the `Register` augmentation, as above, and `export const localeCookie = cookieDetector('NEXT_LOCALE')`. The language switcher calls `localeCookie.persist?.(next)` before navigating.
- `src/proxy.ts`: redirect `/path` to `/{locale}/path`, choosing the locale with `i18n.match(request.cookies.get('NEXT_LOCALE')?.value) ?? negotiateLocale(request.headers.get('accept-language'), i18n.locales, i18n.defaultLocale)`.
- `src/app/[lang]/layout.tsx`: `generateStaticParams = () => i18n.locales.map(lang => ({ lang }))`. Call `notFound()` unless `i18n.match(lang) === lang`. Render `<html lang={lang} dir={getDirection(lang)}>`.
- `src/app/[lang]/providers.tsx` (`'use client'`): `<I18nProvider i18n={i18n} locale={lang}>`. Import the instance in this client file; it can't be passed as a prop from the server.
- Server Components: `const translate = await i18n.loadTranslator(lang)`, or `i18n.loadTranslator(lang, 'home')` for a namespace. Use `translate()` and `translate.rich()`.
- Client Components: `useTranslator()`. Switch language by navigating to the other locale's URL.
